source.revisionRole: Provenance reference for the initial survey only; not a development pin.
source.reviewMethod: Read-only review of all 278 catalog entries against the official OpenKore master checkout at this revision. Compared with the initial survey revision; all 70 referenced source paths exist at the reviewed revision. The only upstream source change since the initial survey was in src/AI/CoreLogic.pm and its queued-loot/auto-attack coordination behavior is reflected in ai.combat-coordination. File links identify supporting locations and do not claim full behavioral parity; protocol-dependent behavior still requires authorized integration fixtures.

milestones.name: Alpha
milestones.objective: First usable combat and gathering release

features.title: Authentication
features.description: A selected server profile supplies the account endpoint and protocol version; accepted credentials advance the connection to the server's next login stage, while denial, timeout, or socket loss leaves no authenticated session.
acceptanceCriteria: Against an authorized protocol fixture, accepted and rejected replies must produce the expected connection states; a timeout/close case must clear pending authentication. Preserve the sanitized packet/state trace as integration evidence.

features.title: Server selection
features.description: The configured server list exposes only usable entries with their login address, protocol type, and required account settings; selecting one binds subsequent login packets to that exact profile.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture with two server profiles must select the requested endpoint and packet parser; an unknown or incomplete profile must fail before a socket is opened. Record profile fixture and connection-selection assertions.

features.title: Character selection
features.description: After successful account login, the client presents only characters returned for that account and sends the chosen slot to the character server; a stale or invalid slot cannot enter a map session.
acceptanceCriteria: A sanitized character-list fixture must preserve slot identity and select the requested character; an out-of-range slot or rejected reply must keep map-server entry disabled. Capture the decoded response and state assertions.

features.title: Map server connection
features.description: A valid character-server transfer response supplies the map endpoint and session credentials used to open the map connection; rejected or incomplete transfer data must not create an in-game state.
acceptanceCriteria: A local protocol server fixture must validate the transfer fields and observe the map handshake; malformed address, denial, and timeout must return a connection error with no synchronized world. Keep the transcript as integration evidence.

features.title: Packet framing
features.description: The byte stream tokenizer emits complete packets according to the selected server's packet-length table, including packets split across reads and several packets coalesced in one read.
acceptanceCriteria: Deterministic byte-stream tests must prove split/coalesced frames produce the exact ordered packet boundaries and that unknown length or truncated input is rejected without consuming later valid bytes. Keep fixture bytes and boundary assertions.

features.title: Packet interpretation
features.description: A packet selected by the active protocol table is decoded into the documented typed event and field values; unknown opcodes or truncated payloads are surfaced without applying a partial world update.
acceptanceCriteria: Golden packet fixtures must assert opcode-to-event mapping and decoded fields for each supported protocol profile; malformed and unknown packets must return explicit errors and preserve prior state. Store fixture provenance and decoder assertions.

features.title: Session synchronization
features.description: Login, character, and map transitions update one coherent session state only after corresponding server responses; duplicate or late packets cannot move a closed session backward or mark an incomplete session active.
acceptanceCriteria: A scripted packet sequence must assert the allowed state transition after each reply and ignore/reject stale sequence events; disconnect between stages must leave no authenticated character or map state. Retain ordered event trace.

features.title: Automatic reconnection
features.description: When an established connection is lost and retry is enabled, the client retries the configured endpoint under the configured retry policy and resumes only after a fresh server handshake.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic clock/socket fixture must assert retry scheduling, bounded attempts/backoff, and a successful reconnect path; disabling retry or exhausting attempts must expose a disconnected state without duplicate sessions. Save event and timer assertions.

features.title: Relog
features.description: The relog command closes the current session and starts the configured login sequence again after its requested delay; it does not reuse a stale map or character session token.
acceptanceCriteria: Command tests with a fake clock must assert close-before-login ordering and the selected delay; cancellation or failed login must remain disconnected and report the failure. Record command input and emitted state events.

features.title: Disconnection handling
features.description: A socket close, server disconnect packet, or protocol timeout terminates the affected connection and reports the reason while clearing only state owned by that connection.
acceptanceCriteria: Integration fixtures for each disconnect cause must assert one terminal event, released socket/task resources, and no false in-game status; repeated close notifications must not duplicate recovery actions. Keep sanitized traces.

features.title: Session recovery
features.description: After a recoverable disconnect, the client reconstructs login progress from fresh server responses rather than restoring stale transient tokens or character coordinates.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic staged-session test must interrupt at account, character, and map stages and assert recovery resumes from the first valid stage; unrecoverable authentication errors must stop retry and explain the failure. Preserve state-machine test output.

features.title: Character creation
features.description: Character creation sends the requested appearance and slot fields to a server profile that supports creation and reports the server's accepted character record; validation failure does not select a nonexistent character.
acceptanceCriteria: Against an authorized test server, submit valid and invalid creation requests and assert the returned slot/identity or rejection; no local character is added before server confirmation. Keep sanitized request/response evidence.

features.title: PIN
features.description: When the selected server requires a PIN, the client sends the PIN challenge response using that profile's supported exchange and proceeds only on server acceptance.
acceptanceCriteria: A protocol fixture must exercise accepted PIN, rejected PIN, and timeout responses; only acceptance may continue authentication, and the PIN must not appear in logs or persisted diagnostics. Retain redacted integration trace.

features.title: OTP
features.description: For a server profile that requests a one-time code, the client prompts or obtains the configured OTP input and sends it in the corresponding authentication stage; rejection or expiry returns to an unauthenticated state.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized protocol fixture must exercise OTP challenge, valid response, invalid response, and expired response; assert stage ordering and that secrets are redacted. Store the sanitized exchange trace.

features.title: Server transitions
features.description: When the server directs the character between supported server endpoints, the client closes the previous transport and establishes the newly advertised endpoint with the supplied session context.
acceptanceCriteria: A two-endpoint protocol fixture must assert close/open ordering and preserve character identity only after acceptance; invalid transfer data or denial must not leave both transports active. Keep transition trace.

features.title: Multiple protocol versions
features.description: Each declared protocol profile selects its own packet identifiers, lengths, and encodings; a packet valid in one profile is not silently decoded with another profile's rules.
acceptanceCriteria: For every claimed version, golden fixtures must decode to the same semantic event where applicable and reject a cross-version mismatch; store the profile-to-fixture matrix and test output.

features.title: Server profiles
features.description: A named profile supplies a complete, validated set of endpoint, protocol, and region settings and is selected as one unit for connection and decoding.
acceptanceCriteria: Profile parsing tests must load two distinct profiles and assert endpoint/parser selection; missing required values and duplicate names must be reported before network startup. Preserve redacted profile fixtures.

features.title: Authorized proxy modes
features.description: A proxy mode is enabled only when the operator explicitly configures the supported local forwarding endpoint; it forwards permitted client traffic while preserving packet boundaries and reports upstream loss.
acceptanceCriteria: A loopback client/server integration test must verify bidirectional byte preservation and disconnect propagation; invalid bind targets or disabled proxy mode must not open a listener. Keep a local trace and configuration fixture.

features.title: Position
features.description: The character's position is the last coordinate confirmed by a server movement or map-state event, not the most recently requested destination; map changes reset coordinates to the new field context.
acceptanceCriteria: Feed movement request, acknowledgment, rejection, and map-change fixtures into the state reducer; assert only confirmed coordinates become current and old-map positions are discarded. Keep the deterministic event sequence and resulting state.

features.title: HP/SP
features.description: Character HP and SP reflect the latest server values and remain within the protocol's reported maxima; missing or stale updates do not fabricate recovery.
acceptanceCriteria: Apply full, partial, duplicate, and out-of-order status fixtures and assert current/max values and update ordering; invalid ranges are rejected without replacing the last valid status. Preserve table-driven state assertions.

features.title: Character identification
features.description: The session binds server-provided character identity and slot metadata to the active character and clears that identity when the session ends.
acceptanceCriteria: A login fixture must assert the selected server identity fields match the active character; a failed selection or disconnect must clear the binding. Save sanitized packet fixture and state snapshot.

features.title: Actors
features.description: Entity updates create, update, and remove actors by stable server identity while keeping actor type and map membership consistent.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic spawn/update/remove stream must leave one actor per server ID with the final fields; duplicate spawns and removal of unknown IDs must not corrupt the list. Keep event sequence and snapshot evidence.

features.title: Monsters
features.description: Monster actor records expose server-reported identity, position, movement, and status needed by targeting and visibility logic; disappearance removes stale entries.
acceptanceCriteria: Monster spawn/move/status/disappear fixtures must update the corresponding record and remove it on the server's disappearance event; malformed updates must leave the last valid record intact. Preserve decoded fixture assertions.

features.title: Players
features.description: Player actor records distinguish other characters from the local character and update name, position, and visible status from server events.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture containing local and remote IDs must not overwrite the local record; remote updates and removal must affect only that player. Keep actor-map test output.

features.title: NPCs
features.description: NPC actor records retain server identity, class/name when available, and position, and are removed when the server removes them.
acceptanceCriteria: NPC spawn, name-resolution, movement, and removal fixtures must produce the expected map index; incomplete name data remains explicitly unknown rather than guessed. Preserve fixture and assertions.

features.title: Portals
features.description: Portal entities map a server-reported source/destination pair to a traversable transition only when both endpoints are known; stale or partial records are not treated as routes.
acceptanceCriteria: A field/portal fixture with valid, missing, and removed endpoints must build only the valid transition and delete it after removal; keep parsed fixture and route graph assertion.

features.title: Attributes
features.description: Attribute updates store each reported base/job attribute separately and apply only server-confirmed values; unknown attribute identifiers are rejected or retained as unknown.
acceptanceCriteria: Table-driven attribute packets must update only the named field and leave other attributes unchanged; unknown IDs and truncated values must produce explicit decode errors. Keep golden packet results.

features.title: Experience
features.description: Base and job experience gains update their separate counters from server values without double-applying duplicate packets.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic sequence of initial status and gain packets must yield exact base/job totals; duplicate or stale events must not increment totals twice. Preserve event stream and expected counters.

features.title: Levels
features.description: A level-up event changes the relevant base or job level only after server confirmation and does not infer a level from experience alone.
acceptanceCriteria: Status/level-up fixtures must assert the correct level and associated points update; a gain below the threshold or duplicate notification must not create a second level. Keep packet fixture and state diff.

features.title: Negative status effects
features.description: Negative status effects track server-reported start, refresh, and end events with their identifiers and duration when supplied; expired or removed effects are not shown as active.
acceptanceCriteria: Deterministic status event tests must cover apply, refresh, expiry, explicit removal, and unknown status IDs; only active known effects appear in snapshots. Preserve clock-controlled assertions.

features.title: Damage
features.description: Damage events attribute source, target, amount, and damage type only from decoded server evidence; malformed or duplicate events cannot alter HP twice.
acceptanceCriteria: A packet fixture must yield the expected combat event and independently reconcile HP status; duplicate display events must not reapply damage. Keep raw fixture, decoded event, and state comparison.

features.title: Death
features.description: A death notification marks the character unavailable for actions and records the server-confirmed death state without assuming respawn or restoring HP.
acceptanceCriteria: A state-machine test must assert combat/movement actions are gated on death and remain gated until a respawn/status response; duplicate death events are idempotent. Preserve transitions.

features.title: Respawn
features.description: A respawn event clears the dead state and adopts the server-confirmed map and position; a requested respawn action alone does not move the character in local state.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic event sequence must remain dead until server confirmation, then set the returned coordinates; rejection, timeout, or map mismatch leaves recovery pending/error rather than falsely alive. Retain event trace.

features.title: Automatic attribute distribution
features.description: Configured attribute targets consume available stat points in the configured order and stop when targets are met or the server reports no points remain.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure allocator fixture must produce the exact ordered requests for multiple target profiles; insufficient points, invalid target, or rejected server response must not be recorded as allocated. Keep allocation and response assertions.

features.title: Automatic skill point distribution
features.description: Configured skill priorities spend only currently available job points on eligible skills and obey each skill's prerequisites and maximum level.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic skill-tree fixture must assert the chosen skill order and resulting levels; unmet prerequisite, insufficient points, or server rejection must stop subsequent requests. Save fixture and request sequence.

features.title: Special states
features.description: Special states are represented only from recognized server status events, including start, update, and end, without inferring effects from unrelated actor fields.
acceptanceCriteria: A table-driven event fixture must assert recognized state transitions and ignore/reject unknown state IDs; end/disconnect clears applicable transient state. Preserve state snapshots.

features.title: Map properties
features.description: Loaded field metadata exposes only declared map flags such as restrictions or movement properties and applies them to route/command validation.
acceptanceCriteria: A field fixture with known flags must yield those exact properties and block a prohibited test action; absent or malformed metadata remains unknown and is not treated as permissive proof. Keep field file and validation output.

features.title: Reputation
features.description: Reputation values are displayed only when a supported server packet supplies them and are scoped to the correct character or entity.
acceptanceCriteria: A server fixture must associate a reputation update with its source identity; unsupported profiles and unknown identifiers must expose unavailable data instead of synthesized values. Retain packet mapping evidence.

features.title: Achievements
features.description: Achievement entries and completion state are taken from server-provided achievement data; unsupported achievement packets do not create local completion records.
acceptanceCriteria: A protocol fixture must map a supported achievement response to the reported ID/progress/status and ignore duplicate completion; unsupported-profile tests must remain explicitly unavailable. Keep fixture and decoder assertions.

features.title: Map field loading
features.description: The field loader resolves the selected map's supported field file, dimensions, and cell data into a bounded grid; missing or malformed fields fail with a named load error rather than an empty walkable map.
acceptanceCriteria: Use a small versioned field fixture with known dimensions and blocked cells; assert exact coordinates and a clear missing/truncated-file error. Preserve fixture hash and parser output.

features.title: Walkability
features.description: A cell is traversable only when the selected field data marks it walkable and it satisfies the movement rules; out-of-bounds cells are never considered valid.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic grid fixture must assert walkable, blocked, and out-of-bounds results, including boundaries; keep the fixture and truth-table test output.

features.title: Pathfinding
features.description: Given a start and reachable goal on a field grid, routing returns a legal path through walkable cells; unreachable goals return an explicit no-route result.
acceptanceCriteria: Deterministic maps with corridors, obstacles, and disconnected regions must assert path endpoints and every adjacent transition; the disconnected case must return no route. Preserve map fixtures and path assertions.

features.title: Movement
features.description: A requested step is sent only when it is legal for the active field and movement constraints; current position remains the last server-confirmed location until acknowledgment.
acceptanceCriteria: With a fake transport and movement packet fixture, assert the encoded target and that position changes only after acknowledgment; rejection, timeout, or map change cancels the pending step. Keep packet/state trace.

features.title: Arrival confirmation
features.description: A task reports arrival only after server evidence places the character at the requested destination or within the explicitly configured tolerance; requesting movement is not arrival.
acceptanceCriteria: A fake-clock movement test must remain pending after command send and complete only on qualifying position confirmation; rejected, interrupted, or wrong-map updates must not emit arrival. Preserve event assertions.

features.title: Dynamic obstacles
features.description: Newly observed blocking actors or field changes invalidate path segments that now collide with movement constraints and cause a safe replan.
acceptanceCriteria: A map fixture changes one cell from walkable to blocked during traversal; assert the replacement path avoids it and no step is issued into the blocked cell. Save before/after route outputs.

features.title: Random walk
features.description: When no explicit destination is active, randomWalk chooses a reachable walkable destination within configured bounds using the injected random source.
acceptanceCriteria: A seeded field fixture must produce repeatable valid destinations and each path must remain on walkable cells; an empty reachable area must return no destination without looping. Keep seed and result set.

features.title: Stuck character recovery
features.description: Lack of confirmed position progress across the configured observation window triggers a recovery action, while ordinary latency or an in-progress step does not.
acceptanceCriteria: A fake clock and movement acknowledgments must distinguish progress from a stuck timeout; assert the configured recovery path and a bounded stop when recovery also fails. Preserve event timeline.

features.title: Lock map
features.description: A configured lockMap constrains route destinations and ongoing movement to the designated field; leaving it requires an explicit supported transition or is rejected.
acceptanceCriteria: Route fixtures must allow destinations inside the lock map and reject outside goals; a server-confirmed map change outside it must raise a policy event and stop autonomous travel. Keep config and route assertions.

features.title: Route recalculation
features.description: When a route edge becomes invalid or the goal changes, the route task computes a new path from the confirmed current position without replaying completed steps.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic event sequence modifies an obstacle and moves the goal; assert the next step starts from latest confirmed location and excludes completed segments. Preserve old/new route fixtures.

features.title: Inter-map routes
features.description: The route planner composes known field paths and verified portal transitions to reach a target map, reporting missing or disconnected map links explicitly.
acceptanceCriteria: A small multi-map graph fixture must choose a valid sequence of maps/portals and return no inter-map route when disconnected; keep graph fixture and selected transition list.

features.title: Portals
features.description: A portal traversal is offered only when the current map/coordinate matches a known portal entrance and its destination is valid; arrival on the destination map is confirmed by server state.
acceptanceCriteria: A two-field fixture must choose the matching entrance and await destination-map confirmation; missing destination or failed transition must not advance the route. Preserve portal fixture and transition events.

features.title: NPC transport
features.description: A scheduled NPC transport is used only when its NPC, interaction steps, and destination are defined for the selected server profile.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized-server integration fixture must exercise the expected dialogue and destination response; missing schedule, menu mismatch, or NPC timeout must abort the route and report the failed step. Keep sanitized dialogue trace.

features.title: Teleport
features.description: Teleport actions consume only an explicitly available supported item or server-approved skill and complete only after a server-confirmed position change.
acceptanceCriteria: A fake inventory plus authorized protocol fixture must validate resource selection and position confirmation; no-resource, cooldown, denial, and timeout cases must not report success. Keep request/reply evidence.

features.title: Save map
features.description: saveMap establishes a travel destination only from a map and coordinate confirmed by the server and applies the configured return policy.
acceptanceCriteria: A command/config test must store the confirmed map/coordinates and route home accordingly; missing destination and failed save must leave prior setting unchanged. Preserve config fixture and route output.

features.title: Warp Portal
features.description: Warp Portal is offered as a transition only when the skill is available, target memo/coordinate is valid, and the server confirms creation or use of the portal.
acceptanceCriteria: A skill-state fixture and authorized server test must distinguish cast request from confirmed portal transition; missing skill, invalid target, interruption, or denial leaves route unchanged. Keep sanitized event evidence.

features.title: Memos
features.description: A memo destination is selectable only from locations confirmed and retained by the supported server behavior; unconfirmed memo slots are unavailable.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized protocol fixture must round-trip supported memo slots and reject an empty/unknown slot; the selected target must not be substituted when the server declines it. Retain sanitized reply fixture.

features.title: Transport items
features.description: A travel item is used only if it exists in inventory, is allowed by map restrictions, and targets a known destination supported by server data.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic inventory/map fixture must select an eligible item and await confirmed map change; absent item, prohibited map, unknown destination, and server rejection must be explicit failures. Keep choice and transition assertions.

features.title: Airships
features.description: Airship routes use only declared schedules, stops, and current server-observed boarding/transit events; the planner must not assume arrival from elapsed time alone.
acceptanceCriteria: A supported-server fixture must exercise boarding, stop selection, and arrival confirmation; missing schedule or lost transit state must suspend the route and report uncertainty. Keep sanitized event trace.

features.title: Instances
features.description: Instance travel is scoped to the server-confirmed instance identifier and entry/exit transitions; stale instance state is cleared after exit or disconnect.
acceptanceCriteria: A protocol fixture must assert entry assigns the returned instance context and exit clears it; duplicate entry, expired instance, or disconnect must not reuse a prior instance route. Preserve transitions.

features.title: Portal updates
features.description: New server-observed portal data supersedes stale graph edges only after validation of source and destination fields.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic update fixture must add, change, and remove a portal edge while unrelated edges remain stable; malformed update must preserve prior graph. Keep graph diff output.

features.title: Travel costs
features.description: Route cost totals the declared edge, item, or service costs using known inputs and marks routes with unknown cost instead of assigning zero.
acceptanceCriteria: A table-driven graph must verify exact cost sums and route choice; unknown or overflowing costs must produce an explicit unknown/error result. Preserve graph fixture and totals.

features.title: Alternative routes
features.description: When the preferred route is blocked or unavailable, the planner returns the next legal route ranked by declared cost and constraints, or an explicit no-route result.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic graph with a blocked preferred edge and two alternatives must assert the selected legal path and ordering; when all paths fail, return no route. Keep graph fixture and result.

features.title: Target selection
features.description: The combat decision selects an eligible visible hostile actor using configured target filters and stable priority rules; dead, friendly, removed, or disallowed actors are never selected.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic actor set with mixed hostility, distance, and priority must produce the expected target; removal or death of the winner must select the next eligible actor or return no target. Preserve actor fixture and decision trace.

features.title: Physical attacks
features.description: A physical attack command is issued only for a live eligible target within the server-reported attack state and after any required approach; completion is confirmed by combat events, not by command send.
acceptanceCriteria: A combat event fixture must assert command gating, accepted attack response, and target/HP reconciliation; range failure, target removal, or server rejection must not report a hit. Keep sanitized event sequence.

features.title: Approach
features.description: When a target lies beyond usable attack range, movement selects a reachable position that satisfies range and walkability without crossing obstacles.
acceptanceCriteria: Deterministic field/actor fixtures must assert the approach endpoint is walkable and within attack range; blocked target or no legal path must yield a no-approach result and no movement command. Preserve positions and route.

features.title: Attack range
features.description: The attack decision compares confirmed character-to-target distance with the active weapon or skill range and does not attack outside that range.
acceptanceCriteria: Boundary tests at range-minus-one, exact range, and range-plus-one must match the declared metric; unknown range must defer action rather than assume melee reach. Keep table-driven distance assertions.

features.title: Monster priorities
features.description: Configured monster rules rank only eligible targets, honoring explicit ignore, attack, and priority entries before fallback order.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture with overlapping allow/ignore/priority rules must yield a deterministic ordered target list; conflicting or malformed rules are reported and cannot elevate an ignored monster. Preserve rule fixture and ranked output.

features.title: Line of sight
features.description: Ranged attacks or skills are permitted only when the map's line-of-sight rule confirms the segment is unobstructed.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic grid fixture must accept clear lines and reject lines blocked by each relevant obstacle; out-of-map or missing visibility data must fail closed. Keep field fixtures and visibility results.

features.title: Target switching
features.description: The active target changes only when it becomes invalid, a configured priority rule requires a switch, or the operator requests one; the previous target's action is cancelled first.
acceptanceCriteria: A fake combat sequence must assert switch reasons, cancel-before-select ordering, and no switch on irrelevant actor updates; rejected new targets leave a safe no-target state. Preserve event trace.

features.title: Give up on a target
features.description: The controller abandons a target only after a configured condition such as unreachable path, timeout, or explicit filter and records why it stopped pursuing it.
acceptanceCriteria: Clock/route fixtures must trigger each enabled give-up condition and avoid premature abandonment when progress occurs; the next decision must not immediately reacquire an ignored target. Keep reason and target-selection assertions.

features.title: Advanced positioning
features.description: The planner chooses a legal combat position satisfying configured distance, obstacle, and hazard constraints rather than moving directly onto the target.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic arena fixture must compare candidate tiles and select one meeting all constraints; if none exist, combat pauses and reports no valid position. Preserve map fixture and selected coordinates.

features.title: Ranged combat
features.description: A ranged action uses the equipped weapon/ammunition and requires visible target, valid range, and sufficient resources before sending an attack.
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory, range, and visibility fixtures must allow a valid shot and reject missing ammunition, blocked line, and out-of-range cases without consuming resources locally. Keep decision and server response assertions.

features.title: Kiting
features.description: Kiting alternates a confirmed ranged action with movement that increases separation while preserving a reachable safe route and the configured attack window.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic actor/field sequence must show attack only when range conditions are met and retreat only after action/position events; blocked retreat or lost target stops the loop. Preserve timeline and route results.

features.title: Tank mode
features.description: tankMode selects the configured protection behavior for eligible allies or targets and does not redirect attacks toward unrelated actors.
acceptanceCriteria: A party/combat fixture must exercise matching and nonmatching entities and verify only the configured target is protected; stale party membership or invalid target disables tank action. Keep config and decision trace.

features.title: Conditional equipment
features.description: Equipment changes occur only when the active condition matches, the item is present, and the server confirms the switch; combat does not assume an unacknowledged item is equipped.
acceptanceCriteria: A rule fixture must verify match/no-match cases and server acknowledgment updates; missing item, conflicting rules, or denial preserves confirmed equipment state. Save rule and response assertions.

features.title: Cooperative combat
features.description: Group combat uses only current party/actor observations to avoid duplicate or conflicting target assignments and honors each character's independent authorization.
acceptanceCriteria: A multi-actor simulation must assert deterministic assignment and release on death/disconnect; stale member state or unavailable target must not cause an attack command. Retain simulation trace.

features.title: Advanced attack conditions
features.description: Advanced attack conditions are evaluated from typed current facts and produce a documented allow/deny reason before any attack is sent.
acceptanceCriteria: Table-driven condition fixtures must cover each supported operator, missing fact, and conflict; only a true condition emits an action, while evaluation errors fail closed. Keep condition inputs and decision results.

features.title: Targeted skills
features.description: A targeted skill request names the intended actor and is sent only when the skill is learned, available, and the target satisfies its target type.
acceptanceCriteria: Skill-state and packet fixtures must assert the encoded target ID and accepted effect event; unknown target, insufficient resource, cooldown, and server rejection must not be reported as a cast. Keep sanitized packet trace.

features.title: Coordinate-targeted skills
features.description: A ground-targeted skill uses a validated map coordinate and respects its area and field restrictions; it does not substitute the character's current target coordinates.
acceptanceCriteria: Coordinate boundary fixtures must assert accepted encoding within map bounds and reject out-of-bounds or forbidden cells; an authorized server response must confirm cast effect. Preserve fixture and response evidence.

features.title: Offensive skills
features.description: An offensive skill is chosen only when its configured condition, target eligibility, resource cost, range, and cooldown all pass.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic rule fixture must identify the selected skill and exact cost checks; rejected casts and unmet conditions must leave the attack task active without claiming damage. Keep decision table and event result.

features.title: Self-healing
features.description: A self-heal is considered when the configured HP/SP condition is met and the skill is available; success is recognized only from server status change.
acceptanceCriteria: A fake-status sequence must trigger at the threshold and not above it; a protocol fixture must confirm HP/SP changes, while insufficient resource or interruption leaves the prior status. Save threshold and packet assertions.

features.title: Self buffs
features.description: Configured self-buffs are applied only when their status is absent or due for refresh and the character meets the skill's resource/prerequisite rules.
acceptanceCriteria: Clock-controlled status fixtures must prevent duplicate casts while active and schedule a refresh only at the configured boundary; denied/interrupted casts remain pending or error. Keep status and cast trace.

features.title: Cooldowns
features.description: Skill availability becomes blocked for the server-reported or configured cooldown interval and becomes available only when the interval expires or a reset event is received.
acceptanceCriteria: Fake-clock tests must verify unavailable just before expiry and available at expiry; duplicate casts cannot bypass the timer, and a disconnect does not falsely clear a server-confirmed cooldown. Retain timeline.

features.title: Cast time
features.description: A cast remains pending for its reported or configured duration and is complete only after the server confirms success; interruption or cancellation terminates it without applying an effect.
acceptanceCriteria: A clock-controlled cast fixture must assert start, completion, and interrupted paths; the effect event must be absent after cancellation. Keep event ordering evidence.

features.title: Combos
features.description: A combo executes the next skill only when the previous skill's server response satisfies the combo transition and each skill remains eligible.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic two/three-skill sequence must assert response-driven ordering; timeout, denial, target change, or missing resource terminates the combo without sending later steps. Preserve sequence trace.

features.title: Party skills
features.description: A party skill targets only eligible current party members under its configured condition and never treats nonmembers as recipients.
acceptanceCriteria: A party membership fixture plus authorized protocol test must verify recipient selection and server-confirmed effects; stale membership and rejected cast must not be recorded as success. Keep sanitized packet trace.

features.title: Monster skills
features.description: Configured monster-skill rules trigger only for matching observed monster events and honor target, range, and resource constraints.
acceptanceCriteria: A synthetic monster event stream must exercise matching and nonmatching rules; a server fixture confirms the cast, while stale actor IDs or unavailable resources suppress it. Preserve rule fixture and outcomes.

features.title: Advanced conditions
features.description: Skill conditions evaluate only supported fields and operators against a consistent snapshot; unknown fields or malformed expressions return an explicit configuration error.
acceptanceCriteria: A table-driven parser/evaluator suite must assert known true/false expressions and reject unknown names, malformed syntax, and missing required values without casting. Keep expression fixtures and diagnostics.

features.title: Equipment requirements
features.description: A skill cast is eligible only when required equipment is confirmed equipped and its prerequisites are met.
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory/status fixtures must distinguish confirmed versus merely requested equipment; unmet equipment blocks the cast, and a server cast rejection remains an error. Preserve equipment/decision snapshots.

features.title: Interruptions
features.description: A server interruption, movement, cancellation, or timeout ends the pending cast exactly once and prevents subsequent logic from assuming the skill effect occurred.
acceptanceCriteria: Event-sequence tests must cover each interruption cause and assert one terminal cast state with no effect event; a late completion packet must be treated as stale. Keep ordered trace.

features.title: Special class skills
features.description: Class-specific skills are exposed only for classes and protocol profiles with verified skill metadata, target rules, and resource costs.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-profile skill fixtures must assert supported class/skill combinations and reject unsupported IDs without sending a packet; supported casts require server confirmation. Store profile matrix and packet evidence.

features.title: Persistent skills
features.description: Persistent effects remain active while server status confirms them and are refreshed or stopped according to explicit configuration, not a local timer alone.
acceptanceCriteria: Status event tests must cover activation, refresh, expiry, disconnect, and explicit stop; a cast request alone must not mark persistence active. Keep clocked state transitions.

features.title: Option selection
features.description: A skill choice resolves from the configured option list to a valid protocol option for that skill and target; unknown options are rejected before transmission.
acceptanceCriteria: Option parsing tests must map each supported value to its expected packet field and reject misspellings or unsupported combinations; preserve mapping table and encoded-packet assertions.

features.title: Broad skill block compatibility
features.description: Supported skill blocks retain their documented OpenKore control fields, ordering, default behavior, and condition semantics for the declared compatibility subset.
acceptanceCriteria: Compatibility fixtures extracted from supported control blocks must parse and make the same eligible/ineligible decision; unsupported fields are reported by name and cannot be silently ignored. Keep fixture provenance and comparison output.

features.title: Scheduler
features.description: The scheduler selects a runnable decision task from current session events without blocking the network loop and preserves deterministic ordering for equal-priority work.
acceptanceCriteria: A fake-clock/event-loop test must show queued work runs in declared order and event processing remains available while a task waits; task failure is surfaced without starving later safe work. Keep scheduler trace.

features.title: Task queue
features.description: Queued actions retain their declared dependencies and are executed once only after prerequisites complete; cancellation removes pending work and releases owned resources.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic queue fixture must assert dependency ordering, exactly-once completion, and cancellation of queued/running tasks; failed prerequisite must prevent dependent execution. Preserve queue trace.

features.title: Automatic AI mode
features.description: Automatic mode starts eligible configured routines after session synchronization and stops issuing actions when the session becomes invalid.
acceptanceCriteria: State-machine tests must start automation only after a confirmed in-game state and stop on disconnect/death/pause; record action and state ordering.

features.title: Manual AI mode
features.description: Manual mode accepts explicit operator actions but does not launch autonomous target, movement, or item loops.
acceptanceCriteria: A command-routing test must allow a permitted manual action and prove background automation remains idle; switching modes cancels outstanding automatic tasks. Keep task-state assertions.

features.title: AI off mode
features.description: AI off mode issues no autonomous game actions and cancels or pauses active automation tasks without closing the user's session.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic event stream with AI off must produce zero autonomous commands; queued tasks must be stopped and no delayed action may fire after mode change. Preserve command log.

features.title: Cancellation
features.description: Cancellation propagates to child tasks, pending timers, and transport requests and leaves each task in one terminal cancelled state.
acceptanceCriteria: Nested-task tests must cancel at each stage and assert no child or timer sends later work; repeated cancellation is idempotent. Keep task lifecycle output.

features.title: Timeouts
features.description: A task timeout uses an injected monotonic clock and reports the timed-out operation while cancelling its pending work.
acceptanceCriteria: Fake-clock tests must prove completion before deadline succeeds and expiry at deadline times out once; a late response cannot revive the task. Preserve event timestamps.

features.title: Priorities
features.description: Configured priorities order eligible tasks consistently while respecting hard safety constraints and preventing starvation of lower-priority work.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic scheduler fixture with competing tasks must match expected priority/tie order and aging policy; invalid priority configuration is rejected before scheduling. Keep schedule trace.

features.title: HP/SP recovery
features.description: Configured HP/SP thresholds trigger the selected recovery action using current confirmed status and available resources, then wait for server status before clearing the recovery need.
acceptanceCriteria: Threshold fixtures must test below/at/above limits and confirm status reconciliation; no item/skill or server denial must remain an explicit unmet recovery condition. Preserve decisions and response events.

features.title: Automatic item use
features.description: An item-use rule consumes an eligible item only when its condition matches and the server confirms use; inventory counts change from authoritative updates.
acceptanceCriteria: A mocked inventory/status sequence must trigger exactly at configured conditions and reconcile quantity only after server response; absent item or denial cannot report recovery. Keep inventory diff and packet result.

features.title: Resting
features.description: Resting begins only when configured safety conditions permit and stops on a relevant threat, movement request, or recovery threshold event.
acceptanceCriteria: A fake event/clock test must enter and leave rest at the declared conditions; hostile actor appearance or invalid map state must cancel rest before another autonomous action. Preserve timeline.

features.title: Error recovery
features.description: Recoverable task errors invoke bounded, category-specific recovery while fatal/auth/configuration errors stop automation and remain visible to the operator.
acceptanceCriteria: Injected error tests must assert retry only for declared recoverable classes, bounded attempts, and stop behavior for fatal errors; retain error classification and recovery trace.

features.title: Combat coordination
features.description: Combat actions yield or resume according to target state, movement readiness, cast completion, and queued loot work so automation does not issue incompatible concurrent commands or preempt an active collection task.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic task-queue fixture must show that a configured automatic take/gather mode with matching loot work queued suppresses a new auto-attack until that work drains, while no matching queued loot leaves attack eligibility governed by target and timeout rules. Preserve the config, queue trace, and dispatch assertions.

features.title: Navigation coordination
features.description: Navigation owns movement until the destination is confirmed or the route is cancelled; combat, dialogs, or map changes suspend or replan movement explicitly.
acceptanceCriteria: A multi-event simulation must assert no stale step after target/map/dialog changes and completion only after arrival confirmation; save event/route trace.

features.title: Storage coordination
features.description: Storage actions run only at a confirmed storage interaction state and suspend unrelated automation until item counts are reconciled or the storage task fails.
acceptanceCriteria: A fake NPC/storage exchange must verify open, transfer, reconcile, close ordering; disconnect or menu mismatch must stop the routine without claiming final counts. Keep state and inventory diffs.

features.title: Buying coordination
features.description: Purchase actions use the active buy rule, budget, inventory capacity, and current currency, and wait for server-reported inventory/currency changes.
acceptanceCriteria: A transaction fixture must compute eligible quantity and reconcile the server reply; insufficient funds, capacity, or refusal must leave purchase incomplete. Preserve request and inventory snapshot.

features.title: Selling coordination
features.description: Sale actions exclude protected/required items, respect configured quantities, and update inventory/currency only from server confirmation.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture with protected and sellable stacks must request only allowed quantities and reconcile accepted counts; refusal or partial sale must be reflected exactly. Keep rule fixture and result.

features.title: Automatic configuration switching
features.description: A profile switch occurs only when its trigger matches and atomically replaces the relevant effective configuration before new decisions run.
acceptanceCriteria: Deterministic trigger tests must assert selected profile and no mixed old/new decision fields; invalid profile or failed load must retain the prior active configuration. Preserve profile snapshots.

features.title: Profiles
features.description: A named profile loads its own validated settings and remains isolated from other profiles unless an explicit shared setting is defined.
acceptanceCriteria: Two profile fixtures must produce distinct effective values and switching back must restore the original; missing or malformed profile reports the field and keeps current settings. Keep fixture diff.

features.title: Conditional commands
features.description: A conditional command executes only when its parsed predicate evaluates true against the current snapshot and rejects unknown commands or malformed predicates.
acceptanceCriteria: Parser/evaluator fixtures must show true executes once, false executes zero times, and unknown/malformed inputs produce a diagnostic without side effects. Preserve expressions and action trace.

features.title: Composite automations
features.description: A composite routine runs its declared stages in order, passes explicit outputs between them, and stops dependent stages after a failure or cancellation.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic multi-stage fixture must assert order, value handoff, and failure/cancellation propagation; final success is emitted only after all required stages complete. Keep execution trace.

features.title: Inventory contents
features.description: The inventory view is keyed by server item identity and reflects the latest authoritative inventory snapshot and deltas; items disappear only after a server update.
acceptanceCriteria: Snapshot/delta fixtures must produce the exact item set and preserve unrelated stacks; duplicate, missing, or malformed deltas must not lose items silently. Keep before/after inventory snapshots.

features.title: Item quantities
features.description: Stack quantities are updated from server inventory events and never become negative or exceed the reported stack limit.
acceptanceCriteria: Table-driven add/remove/split/merge events must yield exact counts; duplicate or oversized deltas must return an explicit inconsistency and retain the last valid quantity. Preserve event sequence.

features.title: Weight tracking
features.description: Carried weight is derived from item quantities and verified item weights or the server-reported weight, with unknown item weight represented as unknown rather than zero.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic item table and inventory fixture must match expected total and capacity percentage; unknown weight and conflicting server totals must be surfaced. Keep source fixture and computed result.

features.title: Item consumption
features.description: Item use is allowed only for a present, usable stack and requested quantity; consumption is finalized from the server response or inventory delta.
acceptanceCriteria: A fake inventory/protocol test must assert correct item ID/count and reconcile accepted, rejected, and partial-use responses; no local decrement occurs on send alone. Preserve packet and inventory diff.

features.title: Equipment identification
features.description: Equipment entries preserve server item ID, equip location, refinement/options, and identified state without treating ordinary consumables as equipment.
acceptanceCriteria: Golden inventory packets must decode each equipment field and distinguish equipped, unequipped, and unidentified items; malformed option data must not corrupt other entries. Keep fixtures and decoded records.

features.title: Equip
features.description: Equip sends a request only for a present item compatible with the requested slot and marks it equipped after server confirmation.
acceptanceCriteria: A protocol fixture must accept one legal slot and reject incompatible/missing items; denied equip leaves the prior confirmed equipment view unchanged. Preserve request and response.

features.title: Unequip
features.description: Unequip targets a currently equipped item and updates its slot only after the server confirms removal.
acceptanceCriteria: State fixture and server response must prove successful slot clearing; rejection or late response must preserve the confirmed equipped state. Keep equipment snapshots.

features.title: equipAuto
features.description: equipAuto selects the highest matching configured equipment rule for the current context without equipping a missing or slot-incompatible item.
acceptanceCriteria: Rule precedence tests with context and inventory fixtures must choose the expected item/slot; no match or server rejection leaves current equipment intact. Preserve rules and decision output.

features.title: autoSwitch
features.description: autoSwitch changes equipment only when its declared trigger becomes active and restores or selects the next rule when that trigger ends.
acceptanceCriteria: Clock/event fixtures must exercise trigger enter/exit and competing rules; requests must be serialized and effective equipment changes require server acknowledgment. Keep timeline and slot state.

features.title: Ammunition
features.description: Ranged attacks require the compatible ammunition type and quantity for the equipped weapon, and ammo state changes only from server inventory updates.
acceptanceCriteria: Weapon/ammo matrix tests must allow compatible combinations, reject incompatible or empty stacks, and reconcile consumption after a confirmed attack. Keep matrix and inventory evidence.

features.title: Cart
features.description: Cart contents and weight track server-confirmed cart snapshots and transfers independently from the carried inventory.
acceptanceCriteria: Cart packet fixtures must update only cart records and reconcile transfer deltas; duplicate or rejected transfer cannot double-count either side. Preserve both inventory snapshots.

features.title: Item identification
features.description: An unidentified item remains marked unidentified until a supported identify operation is confirmed by server data; candidate name is not inferred from item ID alone.
acceptanceCriteria: A protocol fixture must transition one item after confirmation and leave it unchanged on failure; unknown identify response must remain explicitly unresolved. Keep sanitized request/response evidence.

features.title: Cards
features.description: Card slots and card identities are retained from equipment data and shown only when the server packet supplies those values.
acceptanceCriteria: Golden equipment fixtures must distinguish empty and populated slots and map known IDs; unknown card IDs remain labeled unknown without altering equipment identity. Preserve packet fixture.

features.title: Repair
features.description: Repair requests target a server-reported damaged item and mark it repaired only after an accepted repair response or updated durability state.
acceptanceCriteria: A local protocol fixture must cover damaged, undamaged, accepted, and rejected repair cases; no repair fee/item change is reported until confirmed. Keep request/result trace.

features.title: Refinement
features.description: Refinement requests respect the supported item/material requirements and use server response to reconcile success, failure, and item loss.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized-server fixture must cover accepted and failed refinement responses and assert exact inventory/equipment changes; timeout must remain unknown rather than assumed success. Preserve sanitized trace.

features.title: Supported enchantments
features.description: Only enchantment types with confirmed profile-specific metadata are parsed and displayed; unsupported option encodings remain preserved as unknown values.
acceptanceCriteria: Option fixtures must decode supported values exactly and round-trip unknown values without mislabeling; preserve the metadata version and assertions.

features.title: Item combination
features.description: Combination actions require a configured supported recipe and all required input quantities, and resulting inventory is accepted only from the server response.
acceptanceCriteria: Recipe/input fixtures must calculate exact required quantities and reconcile accepted/failed outcomes; missing inputs and unknown recipes cannot send a request. Keep recipe fixture and inventory diff.

features.title: Item detection
features.description: Ground-item events create loot candidates with server identity, map position, and expiration state; disappeared or unrecognized entities are not treated as collectible.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic spawn/move/disappear event sequence must expose exactly the active ground items and clear expired IDs; preserve decoded fixture and candidate snapshot.

features.title: Item collection
features.description: Collection is requested only when the item remains visible, reachable, and allowed by filters; possession is confirmed by inventory update rather than pickup request.
acceptanceCriteria: A field/item fixture must route to a valid item and reconcile its inventory arrival; blocked path, item disappearance, or server denial returns a failed/expired collection result. Keep event trace.

features.title: Loot filters
features.description: Configured pickup rules classify each item as allowed, ignored, or protected using explicit precedence and the current map/inventory context.
acceptanceCriteria: Table-driven item metadata and rule fixtures must assert each class and precedence; malformed rules fail configuration validation and default to no pickup. Preserve test matrix.

features.title: Loot priorities
features.description: Eligible ground items are ordered by configured priority with deterministic tie-breaking and without bypassing ignore/protection rules.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture with competing item priorities must produce a stable order across runs; ignored items must never enter the ranked set. Keep rule fixture and ordered IDs.

features.title: Weight control
features.description: Pickup decisions stop or change strategy at configured weight thresholds using reconciled current weight and item weight; unknown weight cannot be treated as spare capacity.
acceptanceCriteria: Boundary tests at threshold-minus/at/plus must select expected behavior; missing weight data pauses collection with an explicit unknown state. Preserve inventory fixture and decision.

features.title: Independent gathering
features.description: When no combat or route task owns the character, gathering may select a valid ground item and return control after confirmation or bounded failure.
acceptanceCriteria: A scheduler simulation must prove gathering yields to higher-priority tasks and completes only after inventory confirmation; stale item or no route ends the attempt. Keep task lifecycle trace.

features.title: Greed
features.description: Greed is issued only when the skill is learned, resource-ready, permitted by the active rules, and has eligible nearby items.
acceptanceCriteria: A skill/actor fixture must assert eligible item set and request gating; unavailable skill, no items, or server rejection must not add loot to inventory. Preserve decision and response.

features.title: Storage integration
features.description: Loot policy may route carried items to storage only when a configured storage rule matches and storage access is confirmed.
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory/storage fixtures must select the expected stacks and reconcile storage deltas; failed access or capacity limits leave remaining items recorded as carried. Keep both snapshots.

features.title: Advanced collection rules
features.description: Advanced collection expressions are parsed into supported predicates and evaluated against current item, map, and capacity facts before pickup.
acceptanceCriteria: Expression fixtures must assert matching/nonmatching results and reject unknown fields/operators; evaluation failure prevents collection. Preserve expressions and decision evidence.

features.title: Group collection
features.description: Group collection avoids claiming an item already confirmed collected or reserved by another authorized group member when such status is available.
acceptanceCriteria: A multi-client simulation must assign each ground item at most once and release assignment on member disconnect; missing coordination evidence falls back to safe individual rules. Keep simulation trace.

features.title: NPC detection
features.description: NPC spawn/update packets create a visible NPC candidate at the reported map coordinate; an NPC is removed only on a corresponding server disappearance or map reset.
acceptanceCriteria: A packet fixture must assert NPC identity, position, and removal behavior; malformed updates and unknown IDs must not create a false interactable record. Preserve decoded packet assertions.

features.title: NPC identification
features.description: An NPC receives a stable name only from configured map data or a supported server name response, with unresolved entities remaining explicitly unnamed.
acceptanceCriteria: Fixture tests must map known ID/location to its configured name and preserve unknown labels when no mapping exists; keep data fixture and lookup result.

features.title: NPC dialogue
features.description: A dialogue task sends each interaction step only after the previous NPC response, and completes only on a recognized terminal response.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized dialogue fixture must assert ordered talk/reply events and a final completion response; disconnect, unexpected packet, or NPC loss ends with a named error. Keep sanitized transcript.

features.title: NPC menus
features.description: Menu choices are selected by the server-presented option list and verified option identity, not by assuming a fixed menu index across servers.
acceptanceCriteria: Two menu fixtures with reordered options must select the configured semantic option correctly; unknown/missing choice aborts before sending. Preserve menu and encoded choice.

features.title: TalkNPC
features.description: TalkNPC commands parse the declared NPC target and step sequence, resolve the target on the active map, and stop on timeout or unexpected dialogue state.
acceptanceCriteria: Command parser and authorized protocol tests must assert target resolution and sequence; unknown NPC or unexpected menu returns an explicit step failure. Keep sanitized command and transcript.

features.title: Numeric responses
features.description: Numeric dialogue responses are sent only when the server's current prompt requests a number and the configured value satisfies its declared bounds.
acceptanceCriteria: Prompt fixtures must allow an in-range numeric response and reject text prompts, out-of-range values, and stale prompt IDs. Preserve request/response assertions.

features.title: Text responses
features.description: Text dialogue responses preserve the configured string encoding and are sent only for a prompt that accepts text.
acceptanceCriteria: Encoding fixtures must round-trip supported text and reject overlength or unsupported bytes; an authorized server reply confirms acceptance. Keep fixture bytes and sanitized dialogue trace.

features.title: Quest tracking
features.description: Quest records update from server-reported quest IDs, objective progress, and completion events; command intent alone does not alter progress.
acceptanceCriteria: Golden quest packets must update the correct quest/objective and ignore unknown IDs without inventing completion; preserve packet fixture and state snapshots.

features.title: Conditional dialogue
features.description: Conditional dialogue branches evaluate only from the current NPC prompt and configured facts, selecting a branch whose condition is true.
acceptanceCriteria: A decision fixture with true/false and missing facts must choose exactly one branch; ambiguous or unknown conditions stop the conversation with a diagnostic. Keep rule inputs and result.

features.title: Dialogue failure recovery
features.description: On recoverable dialogue timeout or menu mismatch, the task may retry the declared safe step a bounded number of times and then stop without replaying completed choices.
acceptanceCriteria: Fake-clock transcript tests must prove retries and termination counts; NPC disappearance, disconnect, and non-retryable rejection stop immediately. Preserve step log.

features.title: Instances
features.description: NPC-based instance entry binds the session to the server-returned instance identity and clears it on confirmed exit or expiration.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized packet fixture must assert instance entry/exit identity; refusal, stale entry response, or disconnect must not preserve an old instance. Keep sanitized event trace.

features.title: Mission progress
features.description: Mission objectives advance only from the server's quest/progress events and remain separate from locally inferred kills or collection attempts.
acceptanceCriteria: A quest event fixture must advance the specified objective once and ignore duplicate/unrelated events; preserve before/after progress records.

features.title: Mission rewards
features.description: A mission reward is recorded only when the server confirms the reward and its inventory/currency effects are reconciled.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized completion fixture must verify reward response and corresponding item/currency update; failed claim or timeout remains pending/unknown and cannot be recorded as received. Keep sanitized response evidence.

features.title: Open storage
features.description: Storage becomes accessible only after a server-confirmed storage-open interaction on a supported NPC/map; request send alone does not expose an empty local storage view.
acceptanceCriteria: A protocol fixture must test accepted open and server denial/menu mismatch; only accepted response enables transfer commands. Keep sanitized exchange and storage state.

features.title: Close storage
features.description: Closing storage stops further transfers and clears the active storage context only after server confirmation or confirmed connection teardown.
acceptanceCriteria: A sequence test must reject transfers after accepted close and preserve context after a rejected close until teardown; record response ordering.

features.title: Deposit items
features.description: Deposit requests use quantities available in inventory and storage capacity, then reconcile both inventories against server-reported transfer results.
acceptanceCriteria: A local storage exchange fixture must cover full, partial, and rejected deposit; exact item counts on both sides must match server replies. Preserve before/after snapshots.

features.title: Withdraw items
features.description: Withdrawal requests do not exceed stored quantity or carried capacity, and resulting inventory changes only after the server confirms the transfer.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic capacity/quantity fixture plus protocol response must verify exact allowed quantity and reconcile partial/denied withdrawals. Keep item/capacity assertions.

features.title: storageAuto
features.description: storageAuto applies configured matching rules in order, honors protected items and quantities, and stops when the transfer is confirmed or an explicit blocker occurs.
acceptanceCriteria: Rule fixtures must select exact stacks and demonstrate stop on capacity, access denial, or no match; final counts must reconcile with storage response. Preserve config and inventory diff.

features.title: getAuto
features.description: getAuto selects only configured items and quantities that fit current inventory/weight limits and are actually present in storage.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture with shortages and capacity limits must compute bounded requests; server partial/denial leaves remaining need explicit and not marked fulfilled. Keep selection and response evidence.

features.title: Additional storage types
features.description: A storage subtype is exposed only when the active protocol profile identifies its distinct endpoint, fields, and access rules.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-profile fixtures must decode a declared subtype and reject unsupported subtype packets without merging records into ordinary storage; keep profile matrix.

features.title: Item-based access
features.description: An item-based storage access flow consumes or uses the required access item only when the server permits the interaction, then opens a confirmed storage session.
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory/protocol fixtures must cover required item present/absent and server acceptance/denial; item count and storage state reconcile only from server data. Keep sanitized exchange.

features.title: Command-based access
features.description: A storage command resolves to a known storage action and valid target in the current session; unknown commands cannot issue network operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Parser tests must assert supported open/close/deposit/withdraw argument forms and reject invalid quantities or states before sending. Preserve command fixtures and action list.

features.title: Storage password
features.description: A password challenge is answered only through the configured secure input path and is never written to logs or normal configuration diagnostics.
acceptanceCriteria: A local protocol fixture must validate accepted/rejected password responses and inspect captured diagnostics for redaction; password mismatch leaves storage closed. Keep only redacted evidence.

features.title: Guild storage
features.description: Guild storage is a separate permission-checked inventory whose access, transfer limits, and identity are confirmed by server responses.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized profile fixture must demonstrate allowed access and a denied access case; no guild item is merged with personal storage before confirmation. Preserve sanitized response and separate snapshots.

features.title: Storage failure recovery
features.description: Storage interruption returns the task to a reconciled state using the last server-confirmed counts and resumes only from a safe idempotent step.
acceptanceCriteria: Inject disconnect during open, transfer, and close; assert no transfer is replayed without checking counts and unresolved quantity is surfaced. Keep failure trace and reconciliation results.

features.title: NPC purchases
features.description: A purchase is sent only for an item listed by the current NPC shop and a quantity affordable under current currency/capacity; final stock and money come from the server response.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized transaction fixture must assert selected price, quantity, and reconciled inventory/currency; sold-out, insufficient-funds, capacity, and refusal cases remain incomplete. Keep sanitized transaction trace.

features.title: NPC sales
features.description: A sale includes only eligible carried items and quantities accepted by the current NPC shop; protected items are excluded and currency is reconciled from the server.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture with protected, sellable, and partial stack quantities must request only the allowed set; denial or partial sale must match reported inventory/money exactly. Preserve rule and response evidence.

features.title: buyAuto
features.description: buyAuto applies configured NPC purchase entries only while the correct shop is open and budget/weight constraints allow the requested quantities.
acceptanceCriteria: Rule and shop fixtures must compute bounded quantities and stop at budget/capacity; server refusal leaves the outstanding need visible. Keep selected entries and reconciled totals.

features.title: sellAuto
features.description: sellAuto applies configured sell entries while preserving protected/required stock and waits for authoritative shop results before updating counts.
acceptanceCriteria: A stack fixture must verify exclusions, requested amount, partial sale, and rejection; keep item-list fixture and resulting inventory diff.

features.title: Character-to-character transactions
features.description: A character-to-character trade tracks offer, acceptance, and final server confirmation as distinct stages and records only the completed exchange.
acceptanceCriteria: A local protocol test must cover offer modification, cancel, partner mismatch, and accepted completion; inventory changes occur only after final confirmation. Preserve redacted event trace.

features.title: Vending
features.description: Vending advertises only currently available items and prices under supported profile rules and reconciles purchases from server transaction events.
acceptanceCriteria: A supported-server fixture must validate advertisement fields and one purchase; invalid price, item count, or server refusal must not create a completed sale. Keep sanitized packet evidence.

features.title: Buying stores
features.description: Buying-store offers validate requested items, quantities, currency, and server-supported limits before publication and reconcile fulfilled quantities from server events.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized profile fixture must exercise valid and invalid offers and partial fulfillment; canceled or timed-out stores are not counted as fulfilled. Preserve sanitized offer/response trace.

features.title: Barter
features.description: Barter is available only for a server profile with a documented exchange schema; each offered and requested item is checked against that schema before confirmation.
acceptanceCriteria: A protocol fixture must validate exact item/quantity mapping for one supported barter exchange and reject unknown fields or insufficient stock; unresolved server semantics remain explicitly unsupported. Keep schema and sanitized trace.

features.title: Shop search
features.description: Shop search decodes server-reported listings into seller, item, price, and location records and filters without modifying transaction state.
acceptanceCriteria: Golden listing fixtures must yield exact normalized records and filter results; malformed listing data is rejected and unknown server formats remain unavailable. Preserve fixtures and expected output.

features.title: Bank
features.description: Bank balance and transfer state reflect only server-confirmed transactions and remain distinct from carried currency.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized profile fixture must verify deposit/withdraw amounts and reconcile both balances; denied, partial, or timed-out transfers cannot change local totals. Keep sanitized request/reply evidence.

features.title: RodEx
features.description: RodEx messages/items are parsed from supported server responses and item claims are recorded only after a confirmed claim response.
acceptanceCriteria: A profile fixture must decode message metadata and test claim success, rejection, and missing attachment; item counts update only from inventory events. Preserve redacted packet evidence.

features.title: Mail
features.description: Mail compose, send, receive, and attachment states follow server acknowledgments; unconfirmed sends or attachments are not shown as delivered or claimed.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized mail fixture must cover accepted and rejected send plus attachment claim reconciliation; malformed recipient/attachment data is rejected before transmission. Keep sanitized trace.

features.title: Auctions
features.description: Auction listings and bids are represented from server state, with bid acceptance and final outcome distinguished from local submission.
acceptanceCriteria: A supported-server fixture must test listing decode, accepted/rejected bid, and final result; stale price or timeout must not display a winning bid. Preserve redacted event sequence.

features.title: Cash Shop where supported
features.description: Cash Shop functionality is enabled only for profiles whose packet and item semantics are confirmed, and purchase completion requires server confirmation.
acceptanceCriteria: A profile-specific fixture must verify catalog parsing and one accepted/denied purchase without exposing payment credentials; unsupported profiles report unavailable. Keep sanitized packet/state evidence.

features.title: Public chat
features.description: A public message is encoded using the active protocol's text limits and reported as sent only after the transport/server accepts it; local display does not imply delivery.
acceptanceCriteria: Encoding and protocol fixtures must verify supported character and length boundaries; an authorized server test covers acceptance and rejection, with no log injection from message text. Keep redacted trace.

features.title: Private messages
features.description: A private message is addressed to the selected recipient identity and preserves protocol encoding; a missing recipient or server refusal produces a visible delivery failure.
acceptanceCriteria: A local/authorized protocol fixture must verify recipient field and accepted/rejected responses; message content is not exposed in diagnostics beyond safe redaction. Preserve sanitized exchange.

features.title: Party
features.description: Party membership and member identity are updated from server events, and only confirmed members are used for party automation.
acceptanceCriteria: A join/leave/disband event fixture must produce exact membership and reject duplicate/stale events; keep before/after party state.

features.title: Invitations
features.description: Party/guild invitations are accepted or declined only when the server presents a valid inviter and the configured/operator policy allows it.
